To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the CT findings of diffuse lung disease are determined by (1) the pattern of disease, (2) the location of the abnormality, and (3) the type of lung parenchyma involved.

(1) the HRCT findings of diffuse lung disease can be explained by the underlying pathologic processes; and (2) the pathologic processes of diffuse lung disease are best appreciated by the HRCT findings when the lung is inflated to a transpulmonary pressure of at least 30 cm H _{2} O.
the HRCT findings of diffuse lung diseases reflect the pathologic changes that occur within the alveolar interstitium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathologic basis of the HRCT findings.
the correlation of HRCT findings with lung histology in diffuse lung disease.
the development of a better understanding of diffuse lung disease, with particular emphasis on the pathologic basis of HRCT findings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the radiological diagnosis of diffuse lung disease is based on the pattern and distribution (location and extent) of abnormalities on HRCT images, the correlation of these findings with clinical history, physical examination and laboratory data, and the correlation of the HRCT findings with the pathologic findings.
the radiologist must be able to distinguish between the normal and the abnormal, the reversible and the irreversible, the benign and the malignant.
high-resolution CT is the best available imaging modality for the assessment of diffuse lung disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HRCT findings correlate with the pathologic changes in the airways, lung parenchyma, and pleura.
the HRCT images of diffuse lung diseases can be interpreted in a systematic manner by recognizing the basic patterns of abnormal lung morphology.
the pathologic basis of the HRCT findings is the pattern and distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pathologic changes in diffuse lung disease are often subtle, and the HRCT images are the most useful tool for their detection.
HRCT images are the result of the interaction between the x‐ray beam and the three‐dimensional architecture of the lung parenchyma.
the HRCT findings can be explained by the pathologic changes of diffuse lung disease, and that the HRCT appearance of diffuse lung disease can be predicted by the pathologic findings.
